Filing the lifespan/drain guard as its own OPEN ticket rather than leaving it as a comment here, since this ticket is closed: **4a11-aecf-4d33-45ae** (`digestive-purposeful-quagga`), linked `discovered_from` bug 9f63.

It carries the mechanism (a `with TestClient(app)` in a review-bot test starts the real `reconcile_loop`, the snapshot janitor's filesystem sweep, and a 1200s `shutdown_drain_seconds()` teardown), the A/B that attributed the 99%-hang mode to a diff rather than the runner, and a fix sketch — a shared fixture that stubs the reconciler and bounds the drain, plus a fail-fast assertion when the lifespan is entered without it.

To restate the boundary recorded above: this does NOT reclassify the worker-crash occurrences, which remain unattributed to any diff. It changes the heuristic only — a py3.11 failure is no longer safely assumed to be runner-side, and the two modes are separable from the log alone (hang: ends at a progress percentage, orphaned pytest/python children, no summary; crash: names the test and the `gw<N>` worker). Those want opposite responses, so routing by signature first is the actionable part.
